item.text:
**6B.7 Research Note: Joe Biden in 2024**

Bottom line: **mostly yes.** The 2024 record is much stronger on broad-based, formula-driven allocation than on patronage or punishment. I found repeated evidence of equitable grantmaking, competitive selection, anti-fraud enforcement, and disaster relief distributed by need. The main counterevidence is narrower: student-loan relief was explicitly framed around winning young voters, and critics argued it skewed toward college borrowers. I found **no strong direct 2024 example** of housing, food, jobs, permits, or benefits being withheld from opponents as a loyalty test.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Biden administration spending climate cash fast, as Trump threatens to cancel it | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-18 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/biden-administration-spending-climate-cash-fast-as-trump-threatens-to-cancel-it-3621553 | Reuters quotes the White House saying funds are being awarded “as quickly and as equitably as we can,” and notes the executive branch cannot withhold appropriated money just because it dislikes the policy. That is direct evidence against using benefits as partisan punishment. | 6B.7, 6B.5, 6B.3 |
| Positive | Biden-Harris Administration Announces Next Funding Round of $504 Million for 12 Tech Hubs Across America | U.S. Department of Commerce | 2024-07-02 | https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/07/biden-harris-administration-announces-next-funding-round-504-million-12 | Commerce says the money is aimed at rural, Tribal, industrial, and disadvantaged communities and uses a competitive process. That supports need-based, rules-based allocation rather than loyalty-based distribution. | 6B.7, 6B.3, 5B.8 |

This is a service-improvement example, not a loyalty screen. | 6B.7, 6B.5, 6B.2 |

That is direct evidence of benefits being used for broad welfare rather than political punishment. | 6B.7, 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3 |

Young on Budget Results for Fiscal Year 2024 | U.S. Department of the Treasury | 2024-10-18 | https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2657 | Treasury and OMB framed policy around jobs, lower costs, middle-class growth, housing, child care, health care, and prescription drugs. The structure reads as technocratic and programmatic, not patronage-driven. | 6B.7, 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.4 |

That is the clearest electoral-targeting evidence I found. | 6B.7, 6B.2, 6B.3 |
| Mixed / Negative | AP roundup on student-loan forgiveness | Associated Press | 2024-02-26 | https://apnews.com/article/8a751e085839df0b19c0a599169002cf | AP reports critics said Biden’s student-loan relief skewed toward college borrowers and higher-income recipients, shifting costs onto people who repaid loans or never attended college. That weakens a pure neutrality reading. | 6B.7, 6B.2, 6B.3 |

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find strong direct 2024 evidence that Biden used permits, food, housing, or employment programs to reward loyalists or punish opponents.
- The strongest negative evidence is narrower: **student-loan relief** had real distributive benefits but was also framed electorally, and critics argued the relief tilted toward college borrowers.
- The positive evidence is stronger and more direct in **grant allocation, disaster relief, FAFSA, Medicare drug pricing, and anti-fraud enforcement**.
